design:
Tier 2: the sandbox boundary, reaching both callers of `_decide` (Claude's approve_tool_call and Copilot's _judge) on a Hub's next restart. Hazard: a wrong exemption lets an outside write through, so the exemption is grammar-shaped and narrow. Rollback: revert; no data.

D1 (decided wpc2-a narrowed a, wpc2-b, wpc2-g; operator 2026-10-15). The exemption needs two facts per argument from the PowerShell `_lex`: whether it was wholly one qualifying quoted literal, and whether its pipeline element is in expression mode (first token a variable, a quoted string, a number, `(`, `@(` or `$(`). Inside a script block `{ ... }` each statement is its own element, which is where `$_.FullName -notmatch '...'` sits.
D2. Provider drives are the built-in non-FileSystem set, not 'any <name>:' as the fix plan first said: that would refuse `git show HEAD:README.md`. A drive New-PSDrive creates needs a -Root, which is already judged as a path, so no special case.
D3. Not in scope (wpc2-c, wpc2-d, wpc2-e, wpc2-f stay OPEN): Select-String -Pattern and other pattern positions, refusal rewording, unknown-dialect 'Shell' as PowerShell, bare '/' replacements.

checked: mcp_server.py:2275 _judge_drive_word handles drive letters and Temp: only
mcp_server.py:2338-2340 rule 3 refuses a separator word that expands; _LITERAL_DOLLAR counts
Wire drive on HEAD: Env:PATH, Function:prompt, HKCU:Software allowed; -notmatch '\\.git\\' denied as outside
limits: Copilot's own call path is not driven at home (work PC)

problem: `_judge_drive_word` (`hub/hub/mcp_server.py:2275`) knows drive letters and `Temp:` only, so `Remove-Item Env:PATH` falls through rule 4 as a relative file name and is allowed with the operator told it is inside the workspace (measured with `_decide`, 2026-10-15 sweep G7). Separately, `'\\.git\\'` in `$_.FullName -notmatch '\\.git\\'` is lexed as a word starting `\\`, a UNC root, and refused as outside; `'\\.git(\\|$)'` is refused as an expansion because a single-quoted `$` counts as one (work-PC Copilot drive, run-b175c9ffa621). Combined with F660, a routine file listing ends a Copilot turn.

requirements.rationale: A provider drive names the registry, the environment or the session, never a file in the workspace; calling it inside is false and lets writes to persistent user state through.
requirements.statement: In the PowerShell reading, a word naming one of PowerShell's built-in non-FileSystem provider drives (Alias, Cert, Env, Function, HKCU, HKLM, Variable, WSMan, any letter case), with or without a separator after its colon, MUST be refused as outside the workspace, quoting the word.

requirements.rationale: A pattern a comparison operator matches against is never something the command acts on.
requirements.statement: In the PowerShell reading, a quoted literal that is the right-hand operand of -match, -notmatch, -like, -notlike, -replace (its pattern element), or -split, including their c/i variants, in an expression-mode pipeline element, MUST NOT be judged as a path or as uncheckable. A single-quoted literal qualifies; a double-quoted one only with no `$` and no backtick; one in Unicode quote characters does not.

Every other word keeps today's answer: a command-mode `-match` is an argument and its next word is judged; drive letters and Temp: are judged as today; a New-PSDrive root is judged as a path; the bash reading is unchanged.

in_scope: The PowerShell reading of `_decide` in hub/hub/mcp_server.py
non_goals: How a Copilot refusal reaches the agent (F660)

summary: Under the Workspace posture the PowerShell reading is wrong in both directions: provider drives written without a separator (Env:PATH, HKCU:Software\X, Function:prompt) are allowed as 'inside your workspace' (F601), and a quoted regex on the right of -match/-notmatch is read as a path or an expansion, refusing read-only listings (F661). One change to the judge fixes both.
